text: Preface This book is the consequence of a suggestion that Coale made to Zelnik in 1956 when the latter was a graduate student in sociology at Princeton University.
text_raw:
Preface 
This book is the consequence of a suggestion that Coale made 
to Zelnik in 1956 when the latter was a graduate student in 
sociology at Princeton University.

text: Each student was required to complete a research projectâ€”a second-year paperâ€”and Coale suggested that Zelnik analyze single-year age heaping in the decennial censuses of the United States since 1880 in a manner analogous to Coaleâ€™s work on 5-year age heaping in an article he had published in 1955.1 Zelnikâ€™s analysis showed conclusively that there had been a very nearly linear trend in age heaping at almost every age, for males and females alike, in the censuses from 1880 to 1950.2 The existence of these linear trends made it feasible to estimate single-year age distributions of the native white populations in each census from 1880 to 1950â€”age disÂ¬ tributions nearty free of the effects of age heaping.
text_raw:
Each student was required 
to complete a research projectâ€”a second-year paperâ€”and Coale 
suggested that Zelnik analyze single-year age heaping in the 
decennial censuses of the United States since 1880 in a manner 
analogous to Coaleâ€™s work on 5-year age heaping in an article he 
had published in 1955.1 Zelnikâ€™s analysis showed conclusively 
that there had been a very nearly linear trend in age heaping at 
almost every age, for males and females alike, in the censuses 
from 1880 to 1950.2 The existence of these linear trends made it 
feasible to estimate single-year age distributions of the native 
white populations in each census from 1880 to 1950â€”age disÂ¬ 
tributions nearty free of the effects of age heaping.

text: The success of this early research led to a second suggestion by Coaleâ€”that Zelnik project these single-year age distributions (for females) back to birth to form estimates of white births and birth rates for years prior to the completion of the Birth Registration Area.

by Coaleâ€”that Zelnik project these single-year age distributions

text: This expanded research project became Zelnikâ€™s doctoral dissertation, written under Coaleâ€™s supervision.

text: Upon the completion of Zelnikâ€™s thesis in 1958, it was apparent that two types of extension should be attemptedâ€”births should be estimated from enumerated males as well as females, and the final adjusted birth estimates should be used to determine the approximate completeness of enumeration of each native white age group in each decennial census.

text: INTRODUCTION AND OUTLINE OF METHODS
text_raw: INTRODUCTION AND OUTLINE OF METHODS

text: Anyone interested in the demographic history of the United States, or in using its demographic data, is faced with many gaps and shortcomings in the published population records.
text_raw:
Anyone interested in the demographic history of the United 
States, or in using its demographic data, is faced with many gaps 
and shortcomings in the published population records.

text: One of the most prominent gaps is the lack of an annual series of births and birth rates covering the nineteenth century and the early part of the twentieth.
text_raw:
One of 
the most prominent gaps is the lack of an annual series of births 
and birth rates covering the nineteenth century and the early 
part of the twentieth.

text: A conspicuous shortcoming is inaccuracy in the decennial censuses of population, including incomplete enumeration and inaccurate reporting of age.
text_raw:
A conspicuous shortcoming is inaccuracy 
in the decennial censuses of population, including incomplete 
enumeration and inaccurate reporting of age.

text: These two deficiÂ¬ encies in the data are, in fact, intimately relatedâ€”an annual series of births for some years in the past plus appropriate estiÂ¬ mates of mortality would make it possible to determine the numbers of people who should have been enumerated at various ages in the censuses, since the censuses record the native populaÂ¬ tion by single years of age from 1880 to 1950.
text_raw:
These two deficiÂ¬ 
encies in the data are, in fact, intimately relatedâ€”an annual 
series of births for some years in the past plus appropriate estiÂ¬ 
mates of mortality would make it possible to determine the 
numbers of people who should have been enumerated at various 
ages in the censuses, since the censuses record the native populaÂ¬ 
tion by single years of age from 1880 to 1950.

text: Conversely, comÂ¬ plete and accurate census age distributions, again with the appropriate estimates of mortality, would make it possible to estimate the number of births in the years preceding the census, because the enumerated native population consists of the surviÂ¬ vors of these births.
text_raw:
Conversely, comÂ¬ 
plete and accurate census age distributions, again with the 
appropriate estimates of mortality, would make it possible to 
estimate the number of births in the years preceding the census, 
because the enumerated native population consists of the surviÂ¬ 
vors of these births.

text: Birth statistics purporting to cover the total United States did not become available until 1933, when the Birth Registration Area first included all states.
text_raw:
Birth statistics purporting to cover the total United States 
did not become available until 1933, when the Birth Registration 
Area first included all states.

text: Before that date there are statistics for some states, a few having data extending back to the early and mid-lSOOâ€™s. â€œGeneralizingâ€ these data to apply to the total United States requires the solution of two major problems:

text: (1) that of representativenessâ€”the statistics of these states may not reflect the fertility experience of other states and areasâ€”and (2) the problem of unknown and changing degrees of underÂ¬ registration in those states where records of registered births are available.

that of representativenessâ€”the statistics of these states may not

(2) the problem of unknown and changing degrees of underÂ¬

text: This book is an attempt to fill these gaps in United States demographic data by providing estimates of annual births and birth rates for the white population of the United States back to the 1850â€™s, and by providing estimates of census enumeration errors, by age and sex, for the native white and total white popuÂ¬ lations enumerated in the decennial censuses from 1880 to 1950.3 The general procedure followed is simple in outline: the native white populations enumerated in each of the censuses from 1880 to 19504 were first adjusted for age heaping by single years of age separately for each sex; these adjusted populations were then projected backwards, using appropriate estimates of mortality, to the time of birth.

text: TECHNIQUES OF ANALYSIS AND ESTIMATION
text_raw: TECHNIQUES OF ANALYSIS AND ESTIMATION

text: Fertility and the Birth Rate Standard summary measures of fertilityâ€”e.g., the general fertility rate, the total fertility rate, and the gross reproduction rateâ€”have been devised to minimize or remove the influence of intervening elements such as the age composition that can play an important part in determining the crude birth rate.
text_raw:
Fertility and the Birth Rate 
Standard summary measures of fertilityâ€”e.g., the general 
fertility rate, the total fertility rate, and the gross reproduction 
rateâ€”have been devised to minimize or remove the influence of 
intervening elements such as the age composition that can play 
an important part in determining the crude birth rate.

text: This chapter explains what factors cause a variable relation between a â€œpureâ€ measure of fertilityâ€”the total fertility rateâ€”and the crude birth rate.
text_raw:
This 
chapter explains what factors cause a variable relation between 
a â€œpureâ€ measure of fertilityâ€”the total fertility rateâ€”and the 
crude birth rate.

text: The explanation does not cover all possible demographic circumstances, but it does cover a wide range, including those experienced in the United States since 1800.
text_raw:
The explanation does not cover all possible 
demographic circumstances, but it does cover a wide range, 
including those experienced in the United States since 1800.

text: It provides the needed technical support for statements made in Chapter 4.
text_raw:
It provides the needed technical support for statements made 
in Chapter 4.

text: Fertility Measures Defined The annual crude birth rate is defined as the number of births during a year divided by the average size of the population during the year.
text_raw:
Fertility Measures Defined 
The annual crude birth rate is defined as the number of births 
during a year divided by the average size of the population 
during the year.

text: It measures the fertility of the population as a whole, rather than of that segment of the population biologically capable of bearing children.
text_raw:
It measures the fertility of the population as a 
whole, rather than of that segment of the population biologically 
capable of bearing children.

text: The general fertility rate is defined as births divided by the average number of women of childbearing age.
text_raw:
The general fertility rate is defined as births divided by the 
average number of women of childbearing age.

text: This rate is obviously unaffected by the proportion of the population who are women of childbearing age, but it is influenced by variations in the age distribution within the childbearing span.
text_raw:
This rate is 
obviously unaffected by the proportion of the population who are 
women of childbearing age, but it is influenced by variations in 
the age distribution within the childbearing span.

text: Childbearing performance within this span is described by the age-schedule of fertilityâ€”the proportion of women at each age producing a live birth.
text_raw:
Childbearing performance within this span is described by 
the age-schedule of fertilityâ€”the proportion of women at each 
age producing a live birth.

text: The area under this scheduleâ€”the total fertility rateâ€”is a useful summary measure of female childÂ¬ bearing performance.
text_raw:
The area under this scheduleâ€”the 
total fertility rateâ€”is a useful summary measure of female childÂ¬ 
bearing performance.

text: If the fertility schedule records the childÂ¬ bearing history of a group of women born in the same year (a birth cohort) as they move through life, the total fertility rate is the average number of children born at the completion of childÂ¬ bearing.
text_raw:
If the fertility schedule records the childÂ¬ 
bearing history of a group of women born in the same year (a 
birth cohort) as they move through life, the total fertility rate is 
the average number of children born at the completion of childÂ¬ 
bearing.

text: If (as is more frequently the case) the schedule expresses the fertility of a cross-section of the population during a particuÂ¬ lar period, total fertility can be viewed as the average number of births that would occur to a hypothetical cohort of women subject through its life to the given fertility schedule.
text_raw:
If (as is more frequently the case) the schedule expresses 
the fertility of a cross-section of the population during a particuÂ¬ 
lar period, total fertility can be viewed as the average number of 
births that would occur to a hypothetical cohort of women 
subject through its life to the given fertility schedule.

text: The gross reproduction rate is identical to total fertility except that it sums female births only, so that it indicates the total number of daughters that would be born.
text_raw:
The gross reproduction rate is identical to total fertility except 
that it sums female births only, so that it indicates the total 
number of daughters that would be born.

text: Relations Among Fertility Measures Two factors determine the relationship between the birth rate and the total fertility rate: first, the age and sex distribution of the population, and second, the shape of the fertility schedule.
text_raw:
Relations Among Fertility Measures 
Two factors determine the relationship between the birth
